title: Embeddings rerank — first-run snapshots & UX variants for onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a compact set of first-run onboarding visuals and UX variants for the Embeddings + Rerank quick path. Includes pipeline diagram, annotated screenshots for the Console quickstart, three sample result states (ideal / ambiguous / adversarial), and an accessible text-only walkthrough for email support and docs.
background: PM requested smaller onboarding collateral for the upcoming 2026.03 release that demonstrates end-to-end behavior of embeddings + rerank with minimal surface area. Existing asset sets are large artboards; this ticket creates a compact, mobile-friendly snapshot pack and a text-first fallback to reduce docs friction.
goals: Create 6 annotated screenshots: dashboard entry, dataset ingest, embedding progress, candidate preview, rerank debug overlay, final card list
Design a compact pipeline diagram optimized for responsive docs and in-console help
Produce three sample output scenarios showing how rerank changes ordering and highlights reasons
Include color-contrast and screen-reader copy for all assets
Deliver compressed PNG/JPEG exports and an SVG pipeline for engineering use
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with named frames for each screenshot and an exported asset folder
Pipeline diagram exported as SVG and 2 raster sizes (1200px & 600px)
Three sample output sets (ideal / ambiguous / adversarial) with prompt, candidate list, reranker scores, and final order documented in plain text
Accessibility check: all text at AA contrast, images have alt text, and a text-only walkthrough is present in the design file
Design sign-off from PM (Laila Park) and Eng lead (Diego Morales) captured in comments
pipeline_diagram_notes: Layout: horizontal 5-step flow for mobile first — icons with short labels: Upload -> Embed -> Index -> Retrieve -> Rerank
Visual affordances: use token-length meter above embed step to demonstrate cost tradeoff
Fallback path: lightweight rerank-off variant (uses embedding cosine threshold) shown as dotted line
Annotations: callouts for latencies (median ms) and cost heuristics per step
Export requirements: SVG must be editable layer-by-layer and include IDs for each node for docs animation
sample_outputs: Ideal scenario: query='How do I rotate an SSH key in GCP?' Candidates pre-rerank: [A: rotate-key-docs (0.72), B: general-security-overview (0.58), C: billing-guide (0.04)]. Reranker final order: [A, B, C]. Highlight reason: 'exact match on procedure + code snippet'.

Ambiguous scenario: query='rotate key' Candidates pre-rerank: [X: ssh-rotation (0.51), Y: api-token-rotation (0.49), Z: user-flags (0.12)]. Reranker final order: [Y, X, Z] with short explanation 'API token context preferred based on surrounding doc metadata'.

Adversarial scenario: query='reset password' Candidates pre-rerank: [1: password-reset (0.60), 2: ssh-rotation (0.55), 3: unrelated-ad (0.02)]. Reranker final order: [1,2,3] but UI shows warning pill 'low confidence for top result' to prompt user to expand rerank debug panel.
accessibility_considerations: All screenshot text uses 16px or larger semantic sizes for legibility
Color palette constrained to AA contrast; alternative palettes for color-blind variations included
Each exported PNG has alt text in the assets folder; SVG nodes include aria-label attributes in the exported markup
Provide a text-only walkthrough (300-400 words) to attach to the docs page for screen-reader users
Avoid conveying information by color alone; use icons/labels for confidence and reorder indicators
review_feedback: PM Laila Park: prefer shorter copy on pipeline nodes; change 'Index' to 'Vector index' for clarity
Eng Diego Morales: request SVG IDs for each node and a lightweight JSON mapping for docs animation; flagged potential mismatch in reranker score decimals
Design review (Nora Patel): reduce shadow intensity and tighten container padding for mobile screenshot
Content lead (Jon Ruiz): rewrite final card microcopy to call out 'Why this was chosen' with one-sentence rationale
